```{r download-raw-datasets, include=FALSE}
# Keep source files separate from processed data.
dir.create("data/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Nine raw files needed for this project
files <- c(
  "DEMO_L.XPT",
  "ALB_CR_L.XPT",
  "BIOPRO_L.XPT",
  "GHB_L.XPT",
  "BMX_L.XPT",
  "BPXO_L.XPT",
  "DIQ_L.XPT",
  "BPQ_L.XPT",
  "SMQ_L.XPT"
)

# CDC repository for the NHANES August 2021–August 2023 cycle.
base_url <- "https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2021/DataFiles/"

# Download only files not already saved locally to avoid repeated downloads.
for (f in files) {
  dest <- file.path("data/raw", f)
  if (!file.exists(dest)) {
    download.file(
      url = paste0(base_url, f),
      destfile = dest,
      mode = "wb"
    )
    message("Downloaded: ", f)
  } else {
    message("Already present: ", f)
  }
}

list.files("data/raw")
```

# Abstract

**Background.** This project produced a documented, validated analysis-ready dataset (ARD) for survey-weighted logistic regression of characteristics associated with elevated albuminuria among U.S. adults with metabolic risk factors and preserved estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

**Methods.** Nine NHANES August 2021–August 2023 public-use components were assessed for provenance, linkage, completeness and plausibility, then linked by participant identifier. Diabetes, hypertension and obesity phenotypes were derived from questionnaire, examination and laboratory data, with an explicit indeterminate category. Eligible participants were non-pregnant adults aged ≥20 years with eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD-EPI 2021) and at least one confirmed metabolic risk factor; elevated albuminuria was defined as a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g. Validation re-derived every derived variable, reconciled source values with the original files and checked eGFR against an external calculator.

**Results.** The ARD contains 3,370 participants and 33 variables; all validation checks passed. The survey-weighted prevalence of elevated albuminuria was 10.9% (95% CI 10.0–12.0%). Among 3,270 complete-case participants (401 events), older age, higher HbA1c and higher systolic blood pressure were associated with elevated albuminuria.

**Conclusions.** The ARD provides a reproducible, auditable basis for survey-weighted analysis of albuminuria in this population.

# Introduction
Elevated albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio [ACR] ≥30 mg/g) marks kidney damage, predicts kidney disease progression, cardiovascular events and mortality [@stevens_kdigo_2024; @writing_group_for_the_ckd_prognosis_consortium_estimated_2023], and can precede a decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) [@stevens_kdigo_2024; @gansevoort_lower_2011].

Diabetes, hypertension and obesity identify adults at increased kidney risk [@american_diabetes_association_professional_practice_committee_11_2025; @claudel_assessment_2025]; in this group, albuminuria captures kidney damage that an eGFR threshold alone would miss. NHANES August 2021–August 2023 links questionnaire, examination and laboratory data within a complex probability sample, allowing population-level estimation.

> **Clinical question**
>
> Among U.S. adults aged ≥20 years with at least one metabolic risk factor (diabetes, hypertension or obesity) and preserved eGFR (≥60 mL/min/1.73 m²), which clinical and metabolic characteristics are associated with elevated albuminuria (ACR ≥30 mg/g)?

This project built a documented, validated analysis-ready dataset (ARD) for survey-weighted logistic regression to address this question.

# Methods

## Study design and population

This cross-sectional study used the NHANES August 2021–August 2023 cycle, a multistage probability sample of the civilian non-institutionalised U.S. population. The unit of observation is the individual participant (one row per SEQN).

Eligible participants were adults aged ≥20 years with measured urine ACR and serum creatinine, eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² and at least one confirmed metabolic risk factor (diabetes, hypertension or obesity; Section 3.3). The age threshold follows previous NHANES studies of kidney disease [@kibria_prevalence_2020]. Pregnancy alters glomerular filtration and albumin excretion, so confirmed pregnancy was excluded; participants with missing or unascertainable pregnancy status were retained. Participants with missing regression covariates remained in the ARD (see *Missing data*).



## Source-data assessment
Nine public-use NHANES August 2021–August 2023 component files were obtained from the CDC repository and imported using haven::read_xpt(); the variables taken from each are listed in the codebook.

```{r source-files-structure, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# Group the nine datasets to run the same checks on each.
source_components <- list(
  DEMO_L = demo,
  ALB_CR_L = alb,
  BIOPRO_L = bio,
  GHB_L = ghb,
  BMX_L = bmx,
  BPXO_L = bpxo,
  DIQ_L = diq,
  BPQ_L = bpq,
  SMQ_L = smq
)

# State what each dataset contributes to the study.
source_roles <- c(
  "Demographics, pregnancy and survey design",
  "Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio",
  "Serum creatinine and phlebotomy weight",
  "HbA1c",
  "Body mass index",
  "Systolic and diastolic BP readings",
  "Diabetes diagnosis and medication use",
  "Hypertension diagnosis and medication use",
  "Lifetime and current smoking"
)

# Summarise each dataset before excluding any participants.
source_overview <- tibble::tibble(
  Component = names(source_components),
  Purpose = source_roles,
  Records = vapply(source_components, nrow, integer(1)),
  Columns = vapply(source_components, ncol, integer(1))
)

# Check for missing or repeated participant IDs in each dataset.
# Also check that all IDs appear in the demographics dataset before merging.
source_id_checks <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(source_components), function(component) {
    x <- source_components[[component]]

    tibble::tibble(
      Component = component,
      Missing_ID = sum(is.na(x$SEQN)),
      Duplicate_ID = sum(duplicated(x$SEQN)),
      Unmatched_ID = sum(
        !is.na(x$SEQN) & !(x$SEQN %in% demo$SEQN)
      )
    )
  })
)

# Stop if any ID is missing, repeated or absent from the demographics dataset.
stopifnot(
  all(source_id_checks$Missing_ID == 0),
  all(source_id_checks$Duplicate_ID == 0),
  all(source_id_checks$Unmatched_ID == 0)
)

# Dataset overview table.
knitr::kable(
  source_overview,
  col.names = c(
    "Component", "Purpose", "Records", "Columns"
  ),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste(
    "Overview of the NHANES August 2021–August 2023",
    "source component files."
  )
)
```

Participant identifiers (SEQN) were complete and unique in every file, and every record in the eight non-demographic components matched DEMO_L, supporting one-to-one linkage. Missingness was calculated within each full component before eligibility restrictions.

```{r source-variable-quality, echo=FALSE}
# Check missing values and measurement ranges before selecting the study population.
source_quality_row <- function(data, source, variable, label, units = NA,
                               questionnaire = FALSE, digits = 1) {

  # Stop if the requested variable is not in the dataset.
  stopifnot(variable %in% names(data))

  x <- data[[variable]]
  total <- nrow(data)

  # Distribution summaries for continuous measurements only
  if (questionnaire) {
    min_x <- med_x <- max_x <- "—"
    var_label <- paste0(label, " (", variable, ")")
  } else {
    obs <- x[!is.na(x)]
    # Stop if there are no observed measurements or any are infinite.
    stopifnot(length(obs) > 0, all(is.finite(obs)))
    fmt <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
    min_x <- fmt(min(obs))
    med_x <- fmt(median(obs))
    max_x <- fmt(max(obs))
    var_label <- paste0(label, ", ", units, " (", variable, ")")
  }

  # Calculate missingness using everyone in the source dataset.
  # Count refused and don't-know answers (7 and 9) separately from NA.
  tibble::tibble(
    Variable = var_label,
    Source = source,
    N = total,
    Missing_n = sum(is.na(x)),
    Missing_pct = 100 * mean(is.na(x)),
    Refused_DK_n = if (questionnaire) as.character(sum(x %in% c(7, 9))) else "—",
    Minimum = min_x,
    Median = med_x,
    Maximum = max_x
  )
}

# Apply these checks to the measurements and questionnaire items used in the study.
source_quality <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  source_quality_row(alb,  "ALB_CR_L", "URDACT",  "Urine ACR",        "mg/g",  digits = 2),
  source_quality_row(bio,  "BIOPRO_L", "LBXSCR",  "Serum creatinine", "mg/dL", digits = 2),
  source_quality_row(ghb,  "GHB_L",    "LBXGH",   "HbA1c",            "%"),
  source_quality_row(bmx,  "BMX_L",    "BMXBMI",  "BMI",              "kg/m²"),
  source_quality_row(bpxo, "BPXO_L",   "BPXOSY1", "Systolic BP 1",    "mmHg"),
  source_quality_row(bpxo, "BPXO_L",   "BPXOSY2", "Systolic BP 2",    "mmHg"),
  source_quality_row(bpxo, "BPXO_L",   "BPXOSY3", "Systolic BP 3",    "mmHg"),
  source_quality_row(bpxo, "BPXO_L",   "BPXODI1", "Diastolic BP 1",   "mmHg"),
  source_quality_row(bpxo, "BPXO_L",   "BPXODI2", "Diastolic BP 2",   "mmHg"),
  source_quality_row(bpxo, "BPXO_L",   "BPXODI3", "Diastolic BP 3",   "mmHg"),
  source_quality_row(diq,  "DIQ_L",    "DIQ010",  "Diabetes diagnosis",          questionnaire = TRUE),
  source_quality_row(diq,  "DIQ_L",    "DIQ050",  "Current insulin use",         questionnaire = TRUE),
  source_quality_row(diq,  "DIQ_L",    "DIQ070",  "Diabetes pills",              questionnaire = TRUE),
  source_quality_row(bpq,  "BPQ_L",    "BPQ020",  "Hypertension diagnosis",      questionnaire = TRUE),
  source_quality_row(bpq,  "BPQ_L",    "BPQ150",  "Antihypertensive medication", questionnaire = TRUE),
  source_quality_row(smq,  "SMQ_L",    "SMQ020",  "Smoked ≥100 cigarettes",      questionnaire = TRUE),
  source_quality_row(smq,  "SMQ_L",    "SMQ040",  "Current smoking frequency",   questionnaire = TRUE)
)

knitr::kable(
  source_quality,
  col.names = c(
    "Variable", "Source", "Component N",
    "Missing (NA), n", "Missing (NA), %", "Refused/don’t know, n",
    "Minimum", "Median", "Maximum"
  ),
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
  digits = 2,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste(
    "Missingness and distribution of selected variables in the full source components.",
    "— indicates not applicable."
  )
)
```

Missing medication and smoking responses cannot be read as non-response alone, because question eligibility and planned skips also produce missing values; these items were therefore interpreted alongside their screening questions (Section 3.3). Age, sex and race/ethnicity were complete.

```{r extreme-values-check, include=FALSE}
# Check the ages of participants with the lowest and highest measurements.
# Also check the lowest adult values, since children are not eligible for this study.
extreme_age_row <- function(data, variable) {
  d <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(SEQN, value = dplyr::all_of(variable)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(demo %>% dplyr::select(SEQN, RIDAGEYR), by = "SEQN")

  # Stop if any participant's age is missing after linking to demographics.
  stopifnot(!anyNA(d$RIDAGEYR))

  tibble::tibble(
    Variable  = variable,
    Min       = min(d$value),
    Min_age   = paste(sort(unique(d$RIDAGEYR[d$value == min(d$value)])), collapse = ", "),
    # lowest value among adults
    Adult_min = min(d$value[d$RIDAGEYR >= 20]),   
    Max       = max(d$value),
    Max_age   = paste(sort(unique(d$RIDAGEYR[d$value == max(d$value)])), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Repeat for each measurement to help assess whether extreme values are plausible.
extreme_ages <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  extreme_age_row(alb,  "URDACT"),
  extreme_age_row(bio,  "LBXSCR"),
  extreme_age_row(ghb,  "LBXGH"),
  extreme_age_row(bmx,  "BMXBMI"),
  extreme_age_row(bpxo, "BPXOSY1"),
  extreme_age_row(bpxo, "BPXOSY2"),
  extreme_age_row(bpxo, "BPXOSY3"),
  extreme_age_row(bpxo, "BPXODI1"),
  extreme_age_row(bpxo, "BPXODI2"),
  extreme_age_row(bpxo, "BPXODI3")
)
```
Extreme values were examined at both ends. The lowest blood pressure readings occurred in children, who are present in the source components but outside the study population. High values (e.g., nephrotic-range ACR, systolic blood pressure above 200 mmHg) and the lowest adult values (e.g., BMI 11.1 kg/m², HbA1c 3.2%) were clinically plausible though uncommon, and all observations were retained.

## Phenotype definitions and analysis-ready dataset construction
All variables were derived for the full linked dataset of `r format(nrow(demo), big.mark = ",")` participants before eligibility was applied; summaries below describe adults aged ≥20 years.

### Data integration and participant linkage

Component files were left-joined to DEMO_L by SEQN, retaining all participants. Post-join checks confirmed that identifiers and the record count were unchanged; values were set to missing (NA) where a participant had no record in a component.

```{r merge-nhanes-component, include=FALSE}
# Check that each participant appears only once in each dataset before merging.
source_files <- list(
  DEMO_L = demo, ALB_CR_L = alb, BIOPRO_L = bio, GHB_L = ghb,
  BMX_L = bmx, BPXO_L = bpxo, DIQ_L = diq, BPQ_L = bpq, SMQ_L = smq
)

uniqueness_check <- bind_rows(lapply(names(source_files), function(nm) {
  x <- source_files[[nm]]
  tibble(
    File = nm,
    Rows = nrow(x),
    Unique_SEQN = n_distinct(x$SEQN),
    Duplicates = sum(duplicated(x$SEQN))
  )
}))

# Match datasets by participant ID (SEQN), keeping the variables needed below.
# Keep everyone in demographics; missing matches receive NA.
ard <- demo %>%
  select(SEQN, RIDAGEYR, RIAGENDR, RIDRETH3, RIDEXPRG,
       SDMVSTRA, SDMVPSU, WTINT2YR, WTMEC2YR) %>%
  left_join(alb  %>% select(SEQN, URDACT), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bio  %>% select(SEQN, LBXSCR, WTPH2YR), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(ghb  %>% select(SEQN, LBXGH), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bmx  %>% select(SEQN, BMXBMI), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bpxo %>% select(SEQN,
                            BPXOSY1, BPXOSY2, BPXOSY3,
                            BPXODI1, BPXODI2, BPXODI3), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(diq  %>% select(SEQN, DIQ010, DIQ050, DIQ070), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(bpq  %>% select(SEQN, BPQ020, BPQ030, BPQ150), by = "SEQN") %>%
  left_join(smq  %>% select(SEQN, SMQ020, SMQ040), by = "SEQN")

# Compare participant counts before and after merging to check for added or repeated rows.
merge_check <- tibble(
  Measure = c("Rows in demographic file",
              "Rows after joins",
              "Unique SEQN after joins",
              "Duplicate SEQN after joins"),
  Value = c(nrow(demo),
            nrow(ard),
            n_distinct(ard$SEQN),
            sum(duplicated(ard$SEQN)))
)

knitr::kable(uniqueness_check,
             caption = "Participant uniqueness within each source file")
knitr::kable(merge_check,
             caption = "Row count and participant uniqueness after linkage")

# Stop if merging changes the participant count or IDs,
# or leaves any missing or repeated IDs.
stopifnot(
  nrow(ard) == nrow(demo),
  !anyNA(ard$SEQN),
  anyDuplicated(ard$SEQN) == 0L,
  setequal(ard$SEQN, demo$SEQN)
)
```


### Kidney function and albuminuria

eGFR was calculated from serum creatinine (LBXSCR, mg/dL), age and sex using the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation [@inker_new_2021]; the equation is provided in the codebook. ACR (URDACT, mg/g) was retained as continuous, with elevated albuminuria defined as ≥30 mg/g.


```{r derive-egfr, include=FALSE}
# RIDAGEYR = age in years; RIAGENDR = sex (1 = male, 2 = female).
# LBXSCR = serum creatinine (mg/dL); URDACT = urine ACR (mg/g).

ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    # Set the sex-specific constants for the CKD-EPI 2021 equation.
    # NHANES codes sex as 1 = male and 2 = female.
    kappa = if_else(RIAGENDR == 2, 0.7, 0.9),
    alpha = if_else(RIAGENDR == 2, -0.241, -0.302),
    female_factor = if_else(RIAGENDR == 2, 1.012, 1),
    # Calculate eGFR for adults aged 20 or older with positive creatinine and known sex.
    # Leave eGFR missing when these conditions are not met.
    egfr = if_else(
      RIDAGEYR >= 20 &
        !is.na(LBXSCR) & LBXSCR > 0 &
        RIAGENDR %in% c(1, 2),
      142 *
        pmin(LBXSCR / kappa, 1)^alpha *
        pmax(LBXSCR / kappa, 1)^(-1.200) *
        0.9938^RIDAGEYR *
        female_factor,
      NA_real_
    ),
    # Define elevated albuminuria as ACR >= 30 mg/g; keep missing ACR as NA.
    # elevated_acr: TRUE = ACR >= 30 mg/g, FALSE = below 30, NA = missing.
    elevated_acr = if_else(!is.na(URDACT), URDACT >= 30, NA)
  )
# Summarise available kidney measurements and eGFR values among adults.
# Count how many have eGFR below 60, elevated ACR, or both ACR and creatinine measured.
kidney_check <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  summarise(
    n_adults          = n(),
    n_with_creatinine = sum(!is.na(LBXSCR)),
    n_with_egfr       = sum(!is.na(egfr)),
    egfr_min          = min(egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    egfr_median       = median(egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    egfr_max          = max(egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_egfr_lt_60      = sum(egfr < 60, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_with_acr        = sum(!is.na(URDACT)),
    n_acr_ge_30       = sum(elevated_acr, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_with_both       = sum(!is.na(URDACT) & !is.na(LBXSCR))
  )

knitr::kable(
  kidney_check,
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Kidney function and albuminuria: availability and distribution after derivation"
)
```

### Mean blood pressure

Blood pressure followed the NHANES oscillometric protocol: up to three readings, about 60 seconds apart, taken with an automated upper-arm device after five minutes of seated rest. Mean systolic and diastolic pressures were calculated separately from all available readings, including the first, and set to missing when none was available.

```{r derive-bp-measure, include=FALSE}
# BPXOSY1–3 = systolic BP readings; BPXODI1–3 = diastolic BP readings (mmHg).


ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    # Average the available readings for each participant, separately for systolic and       diastolic BP.
    # Use one or two readings when all three are not available.
    mean_sbp = rowMeans(
      pick(BPXOSY1, BPXOSY2, BPXOSY3),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    mean_dbp = rowMeans(
      pick(BPXODI1, BPXODI2, BPXODI3),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    # When all readings are missing, replace the NaN result with NA.
    mean_sbp = if_else(is.nan(mean_sbp), NA_real_, mean_sbp),
    mean_dbp = if_else(is.nan(mean_dbp), NA_real_, mean_dbp)
  )

bp_summary <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  summarise(
    n_adults    = n(),
    n_with_sbp  = sum(!is.na(mean_sbp)),
    n_with_dbp  = sum(!is.na(mean_dbp)),
    sbp_min     = min(mean_sbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    sbp_median  = median(mean_sbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    sbp_max     = max(mean_sbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    dbp_min     = min(mean_dbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    dbp_median  = median(mean_dbp, na.rm = TRUE),
    dbp_max     = max(mean_dbp, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

knitr::kable(
  bp_summary,
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Availability and distribution of mean blood-pressure measurements among adults"
)
```

```{r bp-reading-counts, include=FALSE}
# Count available systolic and diastolic readings for each adult.
bp_reading_counts <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  mutate(
    n_sbp = rowSums(!is.na(pick(BPXOSY1, BPXOSY2, BPXOSY3))),
    n_dbp = rowSums(!is.na(pick(BPXODI1, BPXODI2, BPXODI3)))
  )

# Check that each adult has the same number of systolic and diastolic readings
# before using the systolic count to report both.
stopifnot(all(bp_reading_counts$n_sbp == bp_reading_counts$n_dbp))

# Calculate the counts used in the report text directly from the data.
n_bp3 <- sum(bp_reading_counts$n_sbp == 3)
n_bp2 <- sum(bp_reading_counts$n_sbp == 2)
n_bp1 <- sum(bp_reading_counts$n_sbp == 1)

# Show how many adults had one, two or three readings.
# Exclude those with no readings because their mean BP could not be calculated.
bp_reading_counts %>%
  filter(n_sbp > 0) %>%
  count(Readings = n_sbp, name = "N") %>%
  arrange(desc(Readings)) %>%
  mutate(Readings = c("One", "Two", "Three")[Readings]) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste(
      "Number of available systolic and diastolic blood-pressure",
      "readings among adults with a calculated mean"
    )
  )
```
Among adults with calculated means, `r format(n_bp3, big.mark = ",")` had three readings, `r n_bp2` two and `r n_bp1` one. Extreme means were retained, because excluding them would remove participants with severe hypertension.

### Diabetes

Diabetes was classified as **present** if any of the following was true:

- self-reported physician diagnosis (DIQ010 = 1), **or**
- HbA1c ≥ 6.5 %, **or**
- current insulin use (DIQ050 = 1), **or**
- current use of diabetes pills (DIQ070 = 1).

Diabetes was classified as **absent** when HbA1c was measured and below 6.5 % and the participant reported:

- no diagnosis (DIQ010 = 2), **or**
- borderline diabetes (DIQ010 = 3) without insulin or diabetes pills.

Insulin use was asked only of participants reporting diagnosed diabetes, and pill use only of those reporting diagnosed or borderline diabetes or prediabetes; this structural missingness was treated as non-informative. In all other cases diabetes status was left **indeterminate**.


```{r dm-derive}
# DIQ010 (diabetes diagnosis): 1 = yes, 2 = no, 3 = borderline.
# DIQ050 (insulin) and DIQ070 (diabetes pills): 1 = yes, 2 = no.
# All three questions: 7 = refused, 9 = don't know; NA = missing.
# LBXGH = HbA1c (%).

ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    diabetes = case_when(
  # Any positive evidence counts as diabetes, even if other answers are missing.
  # Check this first so it takes priority over the rules for absence.
  DIQ010 == 1 | LBXGH >= 6.5 | DIQ050 == 1 | DIQ070 == 1 ~ 1,

  # Classify as absent when no diagnosis is reported and measured HbA1c is below 6.5%.
  DIQ010 == 2 & !is.na(LBXGH) & LBXGH < 6.5 ~ 0,

  # Borderline diabetes: classify as absent when HbA1c is below 6.5%
  # and neither insulin nor diabetes pill use is reported as yes.
  DIQ010 == 3 & !is.na(LBXGH) & LBXGH < 6.5 &
    (is.na(DIQ050) | DIQ050 != 1) &
    (is.na(DIQ070) | DIQ070 != 1) ~ 0,

  # Leave all other cases indeterminate rather than assuming diabetes is absent.
  TRUE ~ NA_real_
)
  )

```



### Hypertension

Hypertension was classified as **present** if any of the following was true:

- self-reported physician diagnosis (BPQ020 = 1), **or**
- current prescribed antihypertensive medication (BPQ150 = 1), **or**
- mean systolic blood pressure ≥ 130 mmHg, **or**
- mean diastolic blood pressure ≥ 80 mmHg.

Hypertension was classified as **absent** only when both of the following held:

- no reported diagnosis (BPQ020 = 2), **and**
- mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure both measured and < 130/80 mmHg.

When a participant reported no diagnosis, the medication item was not asked; the resulting structural missingness was treated as non-informative. In all other cases hypertension status was left **indeterminate**.
The blood-pressure thresholds follow the 2017 ACC/AHA guideline definition of hypertension (≥130/80 mmHg) [@whelton_2017_2018].


```{r htn-derive}
# BPQ020 = hypertension diagnosis; BPQ150 = current blood-pressure medication.
# Both: 1 = yes, 2 = no, 7 = refused, 9 = don't know; NA = missing.
# mean_sbp and mean_dbp = mean systolic and diastolic BP (mmHg).
# hypertension: 1 = present, 0 = absent, NA = indeterminate.

ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    hypertension = case_when(
      # Classify as present if diagnosis, medication use or raised BP indicates                hypertension.
      BPQ020 == 1 |
        BPQ150 == 1 |
        mean_sbp >= 130 |
        mean_dbp >= 80 ~ 1,

      # Classify as absent only when no diagnosis is reported
      # and both BP measurements are available and below 130/80.
      BPQ020 == 2 &
        !is.na(mean_sbp) &
        !is.na(mean_dbp) &
        mean_sbp < 130 &
        mean_dbp < 80 ~ 0,

      # Leave all other cases indeterminate rather than assuming hypertension is absent.
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

```

### Obesity

Obesity was classified from body mass index (BMI; BMXBMI) as:

- **Present** — BMI ≥30 kg/m².
- **Absent** — BMI <30 kg/m².
- **Indeterminate** — BMI missing.


```{r obesity-derive}
# BMXBMI = body mass index (kg/m²).
# obesity: 1 = present, 0 = absent, NA = indeterminate.

ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    obesity = case_when(
      # Classify obesity using BMI >= 30; keep missing BMI as indeterminate.
      !is.na(BMXBMI) & BMXBMI >= 30 ~ 1,
      !is.na(BMXBMI) & BMXBMI < 30 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


```

### Combined metabolic risk

The three phenotypes were combined into a single indicator (`metabolic_risk`): **present** if at least one phenotype was present, **absent** only if all three were absent, and **indeterminate** otherwise.


```{r metabolic-risk-derive}
# metabolic_risk: 1 = present, 0 = absent, NA = indeterminate.

ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    metabolic_risk = case_when(
      # One confirmed condition is enough, even if the others are unknown.
      diabetes == 1 | hypertension == 1 | obesity == 1 ~ 1,
      # Classify as absent only when all three conditions are absent.
      diabetes == 0 & hypertension == 0 & obesity == 0 ~ 0,
      # Otherwise, there is not enough information to decide.
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

# Check that metabolic risk agrees with having at least one confirmed condition,
# ignoring comparisons that return NA.
stopifnot(
  all(
    (ard$metabolic_risk == 1) ==
      (ard$diabetes == 1 | ard$hypertension == 1 | ard$obesity == 1),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
)
```
```{r phenotype-table}
# Summarise each condition among all adults before applying the remaining eligibility criteria.

phenotype_table <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  select(Diabetes = diabetes, Hypertension = hypertension,
         Obesity = obesity, `Metabolic risk (any)` = metabolic_risk) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Phenotype", values_to = "status") %>%
  mutate(
    Phenotype = factor(Phenotype, levels = c("Diabetes", "Hypertension",
                                             "Obesity", "Metabolic risk (any)")),
    # Show 1 as Present, 0 as Absent and NA as Indeterminate.
    status = case_when(status == 1 ~ "Present",
                       status == 0 ~ "Absent",
                       TRUE        ~ "Indeterminate"),
    status = factor(status, levels = c("Present", "Absent", "Indeterminate"))
  ) %>%
  count(Phenotype, status) %>%
  group_by(Phenotype) %>%
  # Calculate percentages within each condition, including indeterminate cases.
  # These are sample counts and percentages, without survey weights.
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%s (%.1f)", format(n, big.mark = ","), 100 * n / sum(n))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-n) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = cell)

knitr::kable(phenotype_table,
  col.names = c("Phenotype", "Present, n (%)", "Absent, n (%)", "Indeterminate, n (%)"),
  caption = "Metabolic phenotype classification among adults aged ≥20 years, before kidney-function and albuminuria eligibility criteria")

# RIDSTATR: 1 = interviewed only, 2 = interviewed and examined.
# Count how many adults with indeterminate diabetes did not attend the examination.
not_examined_ids <- demo$SEQN[demo$RIDSTATR == 1]
ind_dm <- ard %>% filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20, is.na(diabetes))
# Calculate the total with indeterminate diabetes and how many were not examined.
n_ind_dm     <- nrow(ind_dm)
n_ind_dm_nox <- sum(ind_dm$SEQN %in% not_examined_ids)
```

Indeterminate classifications largely reflected missing examination data rather than conflicting information. Obesity was indeterminate only when BMI was missing, and diabetes and hypertension could not be classified as absent without measured HbA1c or blood pressure, respectively.

### Demographic and continuous covariates

Age (years), sex and race/ethnicity were retained in their original NHANES coding; HbA1c (%), BMI (kg/m²) and mean systolic blood pressure (mmHg) were retained as continuous covariates.

### Smoking status

Smoking status was classified from self-reported cigarette use:

- **Never** — fewer than 100 lifetime cigarettes (SMQ020 = 2).
- **Former** — at least 100 cigarettes (SMQ020 = 1) and now not smoking (SMQ040 = 3).
- **Current** — at least 100 cigarettes (SMQ020 = 1) and now smoking every day or some days (SMQ040 = 1 or 2).



```{r smoking-derive}
# SMQ020 = smoked at least 100 cigarettes in lifetime: 1 = yes, 2 = no.
# SMQ040 = current smoking: 1 = every day, 2 = some days, 3 = not at all.
# Both questions: 7 = refused, 9 = don't know; NA = missing.

ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    smoking_status = case_when(
      # Use lifetime smoking and current smoking together to classify smoking status.
      SMQ020 == 2 ~ "Never",
      SMQ020 == 1 & SMQ040 == 3 ~ "Former",
      SMQ020 == 1 & SMQ040 %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Current",
      
      # Leave smoking status missing when the answers do not establish a category.
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    # Set Never as the reference category for regression.
    smoking_status = factor(
      smoking_status,
      levels = c("Never", "Former", "Current")
    )
  )

# Summarise smoking status among adults, including those with missing status.
smoking_summary <- ard %>%
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 20) %>%
  count(smoking_status, name = "N", .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = round(100 * N / sum(N), 1)
  )

```

Of `r format(sum(smoking_summary$N), big.mark = ",")` adults, `r format(smoking_summary$N[smoking_summary$smoking_status %in% "Never"], big.mark = ",")` (`r smoking_summary$pct[smoking_summary$smoking_status %in% "Never"]`%) were never, `r format(smoking_summary$N[smoking_summary$smoking_status %in% "Former"], big.mark = ",")` (`r smoking_summary$pct[smoking_summary$smoking_status %in% "Former"]`%) former and `r format(smoking_summary$N[smoking_summary$smoking_status %in% "Current"], big.mark = ",")` (`r smoking_summary$pct[smoking_summary$smoking_status %in% "Current"]`%) current smokers; `r smoking_summary$N[is.na(smoking_summary$smoking_status)]` (`r smoking_summary$pct[is.na(smoking_summary$smoking_status)]`%) could not be classified.


### Eligibility criteria and creation of the analysis-ready dataset
Eligibility criteria were applied sequentially; participants remaining and excluded at each step are shown below.

```{r eligibility-flag}
# Record each eligibility decision as TRUE or FALSE before excluding anyone.
# RIDEXPRG: 1 = pregnant, 2 = not pregnant, 3 = cannot determine; NA = missing.

ard <- ard %>%
  mutate(
    eligible_age = !is.na(RIDAGEYR) & RIDAGEYR >= 20,
    # Exclude confirmed pregnancy only; retain unknown or missing pregnancy status.
    eligible_not_pregnant = is.na(RIDEXPRG) | RIDEXPRG != 1,
    # Require ACR, creatinine and a calculated eGFR.
    eligible_kidney_measurements = !is.na(URDACT) & !is.na(LBXSCR) & !is.na(egfr),
    eligible_egfr = !is.na(egfr) & egfr >= 60,
    eligible_metabolic_risk = !is.na(metabolic_risk) & metabolic_risk == 1,
    # Participants must meet every criterion to enter the study.
    eligible_study = eligible_age &
                     eligible_not_pregnant &
                     eligible_kidney_measurements &
                     eligible_egfr &
                     eligible_metabolic_risk
  )

# Apply the criteria in sequence so each step includes only those who passed earlier steps.
step_preg   <- ard$eligible_age & ard$eligible_not_pregnant
step_kidney <- step_preg & ard$eligible_kidney_measurements
step_egfr   <- step_kidney & ard$eligible_egfr

# Count participants remaining and excluded at each step.
flow <- tibble(
  Step = c(
    "Demographic file",
    "Adults aged ≥ 20 years",
    "Not pregnant",
    "Valid ACR and serum creatinine",
    "eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m²",
    "≥ 1 metabolic risk factor (final eligible population)"
  ),
  N = c(nrow(demo), sum(ard$eligible_age), sum(step_preg),
        sum(step_kidney), sum(step_egfr), sum(ard$eligible_study))
) %>%
  mutate(Excluded = c(NA, -diff(N)))

# Check that counts never increase, the final count matches the eligibility flag,
# and every participant has a known eligibility decision.
stopifnot(
  all(diff(flow$N) <= 0),
  tail(flow$N, 1) == sum(ard$eligible_study),
  !anyNA(ard$eligible_study)
)

options(knitr.kable.NA = "—")
knitr::kable(flow, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "Participant selection flow")

# Separate exclusions due to absent metabolic risk from those due to unknown status.
n_meta_absent <- sum(step_egfr & ard$metabolic_risk %in% 0)
n_meta_indet  <- sum(step_egfr & is.na(ard$metabolic_risk))
```

```{r eligibility-event-summary}
# Check that albuminuria status is known for every eligible participant.
stopifnot(!anyNA(ard$elevated_acr[ard$eligible_study]))

# Count eligible participants and those with elevated albuminuria for the report.
n_eligible <- sum(ard$eligible_study)
n_events   <- sum(ard$elevated_acr[ard$eligible_study])
```

Of the `r format(n_eligible, big.mark = ",")` eligible participants, `r n_events` (`r round(100 * n_events / n_eligible, 1)`%) had elevated albuminuria.


### Missing data

```{r missingness-summary}
# Assess missing data among eligible participants only.
eligible <- ard %>% filter(eligible_study)


# Include the outcome and all predictors planned for the regression.
model_vars <- c("elevated_acr", "RIDAGEYR", "RIAGENDR", "RIDRETH3",
                "LBXGH", "mean_sbp", "BMXBMI", "smoking_status")


# Count missing values for each variable and participants with complete data on all model variables.
n_miss     <- vapply(model_vars, function(v) sum(is.na(eligible[[v]])), integer(1))
n_complete <- sum(complete.cases(eligible[model_vars]))

# Confirm that variables described as complete in the report have no missing values.
stopifnot(all(n_miss[c("elevated_acr", "RIDAGEYR", "RIAGENDR",
                       "RIDRETH3", "LBXGH")] == 0))

# Format missing counts and percentages for the report, using all eligible participants as the denominator.
miss_txt <- function(v) sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n_miss[[v]], 100 * n_miss[[v]] / nrow(eligible))


```
Among `r format(nrow(eligible), big.mark = ",")` eligible participants, the outcome, age, sex, race/ethnicity and HbA1c were complete. Mean systolic blood pressure was missing for `r miss_txt("mean_sbp")`, BMI for `r miss_txt("BMXBMI")` and smoking status for `r miss_txt("smoking_status")`. Complete data on all model variables were available for `r format(n_complete, big.mark = ",")` participants (`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * n_complete / nrow(eligible))`%). The accompanying codebook documents missingness across all ARD variables, including planned questionnaire skips.



### Survey design variables

```{r survey-design-check}
# WTPH2YR = phlebotomy sample weight.
# SDMVSTRA = survey stratum; SDMVPSU = primary sampling unit.
# Check that all three variables exist and are complete for eligible participants,
# and that every weight is positive.
stopifnot(
  all(c("WTPH2YR", "SDMVSTRA", "SDMVPSU") %in% names(eligible)),
  !anyNA(eligible$WTPH2YR), all(eligible$WTPH2YR > 0),
  !anyNA(eligible$SDMVSTRA), !anyNA(eligible$SDMVPSU)
)
```

The phlebotomy weight (WTPH2YR), masked variance stratum (SDMVSTRA) and primary sampling unit (SDMVPSU) were retained and were complete, with positive weights, for all eligible participants.

### Analysis-ready dataset

```{r analysis-ready-dataset}
# Keep the variables needed for analysis and the source values needed to check derived variables.
ard_columns <- c(
  "SEQN", "RIDAGEYR", "RIAGENDR", "RIDRETH3",
  "URDACT", "elevated_acr", "LBXSCR", "egfr", "LBXGH",
  "BPXOSY1", "BPXOSY2", "BPXOSY3",
  "BPXODI1", "BPXODI2", "BPXODI3",
  "mean_sbp", "mean_dbp", "BMXBMI",
  "DIQ010", "DIQ050", "DIQ070",
  "BPQ020", "BPQ150",
  "SMQ020", "SMQ040", "smoking_status",
  "diabetes", "hypertension", "obesity", "metabolic_risk",
  "WTPH2YR", "SDMVSTRA", "SDMVPSU"
)

# Stop if any required column is missing.
missing_columns <- setdiff(ard_columns, names(ard))
if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop("Required columns missing from ard: ",
       paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
}

# Keep eligible participants and the selected columns.
# Retain participants with missing regression predictors for now.
ard_final <- ard %>%
  filter(eligible_study) %>%
  select(all_of(ard_columns))

# Check the expected participant count, unique IDs, eligibility,
# albuminuria classification and survey variables before saving.
stopifnot(
  # Flag any change from the established final count of 3,370 participants.
  nrow(ard_final) == 3370,
  !anyNA(ard_final$SEQN),
  !anyDuplicated(ard_final$SEQN),
  all(ard_final$RIDAGEYR >= 20),
  all(!is.na(ard_final$URDACT)),
  all(!is.na(ard_final$LBXSCR)),
  all(!is.na(ard_final$egfr) & ard_final$egfr >= 60),
  all(ard_final$metabolic_risk == 1),
  !anyNA(ard_final$elevated_acr),
  all(ard_final$elevated_acr == (ard_final$URDACT >= 30)),
  all(!is.na(ard_final$WTPH2YR) & ard_final$WTPH2YR > 0),
  !anyNA(ard_final$SDMVSTRA),
  !anyNA(ard_final$SDMVPSU)
)

# Use the dataset dimensions directly in the report and table caption.
n_ard_rows <- nrow(ard_final)
n_ard_cols <- ncol(ard_final)
```

The ARD contains the `r format(n_ard_rows, big.mark = ",")` eligible participants and `r n_ard_cols` variables:

- identifiers and demographic characteristics,
- the outcome and regression covariates,
- derived phenotypes and the source variables used to derive them, and
- survey design variables.

Intermediate and unused columns were excluded; the dataset was saved as `data/processed/nhanes_albuminuria_ard.rds`.

## Validation

```{r validation-egfr}
# Reload the exported dataset (used by all validation checks)
ard_reloaded <- readRDS("data/processed/nhanes_albuminuria_ard.rds")

# Write the CKD-EPI 2021 equation separately to check the earlier calculation.
# scr = creatinine (mg/dL); age = years; sex: 1 = male, 2 = female.
ckd_epi_2021 <- function(scr, age, sex) {
  female <- sex == 2
  kappa  <- ifelse(female, 0.7, 0.9)
  alpha  <- ifelse(female, -0.241, -0.302)
  142 * pmin(scr / kappa, 1)^alpha * pmax(scr / kappa, 1)^(-1.200) *
    0.9938^age * ifelse(female, 1.012, 1)
}

# Test four examples against reference results from the National Kidney Foundation calculator.
egfr_tests <- tibble(
  scr = c(0.7, 1.2, 0.5, 2.0),
  age = c(50, 60, 40, 70),
  sex = c(2, 1, 2, 1),
  nkf = c(105, 69, 122, 35)
)

# Check that all four calculated results match the reference values after rounding.
check_egfr <- all(round(ckd_epi_2021(egfr_tests$scr, egfr_tests$age, egfr_tests$sex)) == egfr_tests$nkf)

```

```{r validation-rederive}
v <- ard_reloaded

# Compare values, treating missing values in both versions as a match.
same <- function(a, b) all((is.na(a) & is.na(b)) | (!is.na(a) & !is.na(b) & a == b))

# Use numeric values without NHANES labels when comparing.
num  <- function(x) as.numeric(x)

# Identify confirmed yes answers; missing answers return FALSE.
is1  <- function(x) !is.na(x) & x == 1

# Recalculate derived variables from the source values saved in the dataset.
# Compare these with the stored results to check that the derivations agree.
re_sbp <- rowMeans(v[c("BPXOSY1", "BPXOSY2", "BPXOSY3")], na.rm = TRUE)
re_sbp[is.nan(re_sbp)] <- NA
re_dbp <- rowMeans(v[c("BPXODI1", "BPXODI2", "BPXODI3")], na.rm = TRUE)
re_dbp[is.nan(re_dbp)] <- NA

re_egfr <- ckd_epi_2021(num(v$LBXSCR), num(v$RIDAGEYR), num(v$RIAGENDR))

# Reapply the diabetes, hypertension, obesity and metabolic-risk rules.
re_dm <- ifelse(is1(v$DIQ010) | (!is.na(v$LBXGH) & v$LBXGH >= 6.5) | is1(v$DIQ050) | is1(v$DIQ070), 1,
         ifelse((v$DIQ010 %in% 2 & !is.na(v$LBXGH) & v$LBXGH < 6.5) |
                (v$DIQ010 %in% 3 & !is.na(v$LBXGH) & v$LBXGH < 6.5 & !is1(v$DIQ050) & !is1(v$DIQ070)), 0, NA))

re_htn <- ifelse(is1(v$BPQ020) | is1(v$BPQ150) | (!is.na(re_sbp) & re_sbp >= 130) | (!is.na(re_dbp) & re_dbp >= 80), 1,
          ifelse(v$BPQ020 %in% 2 & !is.na(re_sbp) & !is.na(re_dbp) & re_sbp < 130 & re_dbp < 80, 0, NA))

re_ob <- ifelse(is.na(v$BMXBMI), NA, as.numeric(v$BMXBMI >= 30))

re_mr <- ifelse(re_dm %in% 1 | re_htn %in% 1 | re_ob %in% 1, 1,
         ifelse(re_dm %in% 0 & re_htn %in% 0 & re_ob %in% 0, 0, NA))

# Reclassify smoking from the original questionnaire answers.
re_smk <- ifelse(v$SMQ020 %in% 2, "Never",
          ifelse(v$SMQ020 %in% 1 & v$SMQ040 %in% 3, "Former",
          ifelse(v$SMQ020 %in% 1 & v$SMQ040 %in% c(1, 2), "Current", NA)))

# Compare every recalculated variable with its saved version.
rederive_results <- c(
  elevated_acr   = same(v$elevated_acr, v$URDACT >= 30),
  mean_sbp       = isTRUE(all.equal(num(v$mean_sbp), re_sbp)),
  mean_dbp       = isTRUE(all.equal(num(v$mean_dbp), re_dbp)),
  egfr           = isTRUE(all.equal(num(v$egfr), re_egfr)),
  diabetes       = same(num(v$diabetes), re_dm),
  hypertension   = same(num(v$hypertension), re_htn),
  obesity        = same(num(v$obesity), re_ob),
  metabolic_risk = same(num(v$metabolic_risk), re_mr),
  smoking_status = same(as.character(v$smoking_status), re_smk)
)

# Pass only if all variable comparisons agree.
check_rederive <- all(rederive_results)

```

```{r validation-source}
# List the original dataset for each source variable saved in the ARD.
src <- list(
  DEMO_L   = list(demo, c("RIDAGEYR", "RIAGENDR", "RIDRETH3", "SDMVSTRA", "SDMVPSU")),
  ALB_CR_L = list(alb,  "URDACT"),
  BIOPRO_L = list(bio,  c("LBXSCR", "WTPH2YR")),
  GHB_L    = list(ghb,  "LBXGH"),
  BMX_L    = list(bmx,  "BMXBMI"),
  BPXO_L   = list(bpxo, c("BPXOSY1", "BPXOSY2", "BPXOSY3", "BPXODI1", "BPXODI2", "BPXODI3")),
  DIQ_L    = list(diq,  c("DIQ010", "DIQ050", "DIQ070")),
  BPQ_L    = list(bpq,  c("BPQ020", "BPQ150")),
  SMQ_L    = list(smq,  c("SMQ020", "SMQ040"))
)

# Match participants by SEQN and check that saved values match the original data.
# Missing values in both datasets count as a match.
source_results <- vapply(src, function(s) {
  idx <- match(v$SEQN, s[[1]]$SEQN)
  all(vapply(s[[2]], function(col) same(num(v[[col]]), num(s[[1]][[col]][idx])), logical(1)))
}, logical(1))

# Pass only if all source datasets agree with the saved values.
check_source <- all(source_results)

```

```{r validation-survey}
# Check that saving and reloading preserved the dataset and its eligible participant count.
check_reload <- identical(ard_final, ard_reloaded) && nrow(ard_reloaded) == sum(ard$eligible_study)

# Use everyone with a finite, positive phlebotomy weight to check the full survey structure.
survey_frame <- ard %>% filter(is.finite(WTPH2YR), WTPH2YR > 0)

# Check that each stratum contains at least two primary sampling units (PSUs).
psu_full  <- survey_frame %>% distinct(SDMVSTRA, SDMVPSU) %>% count(SDMVSTRA)
check_psu <- all(psu_full$n >= 2)

# Check whether any stratum has only one PSU left after restricting to eligible participants.
psu_domain <- survey_frame %>% filter(eligible_study) %>% distinct(SDMVSTRA, SDMVPSU) %>% count(SDMVSTRA)
n_single_psu_domain <- sum(psu_domain$n == 1)

```

```{r validation-summary, include=FALSE}
# Bring the five validation results together.
checks <- tibble(
  Check = c(
    "eGFR implementation reproduces NKF CKD-EPI 2021 calculator values",
    "All derived variables re-derived from source columns and matched",
    "Source values identical to original NHANES files",
    "Reloaded file identical to exported dataset",
    "At least two PSUs per stratum in the full survey design"
  ),
  Passed = c(check_egfr, check_rederive, check_source, check_reload, check_psu)
)

# Stop if any check fails and name the failed checks.
if (!all(checks$Passed)) {
  stop("Validation failed: ", paste(checks$Check[!checks$Passed], collapse = "; "))
}

# Show each validation result as PASS or FAIL.
knitr::kable(
  transmute(checks, Check, Result = ifelse(Passed, "PASS", "FAIL")),
  caption = "Validation of the exported analysis-ready dataset"
)
```

Validation was performed in two stages. Before the ARD file export, checks confirmed unique participant identifiers, consistency with the eligibility criteria and outcome definition, and complete survey design variables with positive weights. After export, all of the following checks passed: the reloaded file was identical to the exported dataset; an independent implementation of the CKD-EPI 2021 equation matched the National Kidney Foundation calculator for four test cases [@national_kidney_foundation_ckd-epi_nodate], and the stored eGFR matched that implementation; every derived variable was rebuilt from the source columns in the dataset; source values matched the original NHANES files; and every stratum had at least two PSUs in the full survey design, as did every stratum represented in the eligible domain.

These checks support internal consistency, source traceability and readiness for the planned analysis, but cannot establish measurement or self-report accuracy.

Variable definitions, derivation rules and missing-value conventions are documented in the accompanying codebook (`metadata/codebook_metadata.md`; [GitHub](https://github.com/maheration/HDS_M1_NHANES/blob/main/metadata/codebook_metadata.md)).

## Statistical analysis

Analyses accounted for NHANES complex sampling using phlebotomy weights, strata and PSUs. Phlebotomy weights were chosen because blood measurements were required. The design was declared among participants with finite, positive weights, with PSUs nested within strata. Eligible participants were then selected as a survey subpopulation to obtain correct variance estimates, as recommended by NHANES [@national_center_for_health_statistics_nhanes_nodate].

Descriptive summaries used available observations: survey-weighted means and standard deviations for continuous variables, weighted percentages for categorical variables, and unweighted sample sizes. Elevated albuminuria prevalence was estimated with a logit-transformed 95% confidence interval. 

Survey-weighted logistic regression used `survey::svyglm()` with a quasibinomial family, restricted to complete cases selected within the survey design. Prespecified predictors were age (per 10 years), sex, race/ethnicity, HbA1c (per percentage point), mean systolic blood pressure (per 10 mmHg), BMI (per 5 kg/m²) and smoking status. Reference categories were male, non-Hispanic White and never smoker. Model checks assessed events per predictor parameter and added quadratic terms separately for each continuous predictor to explore nonlinearity.



```{r survey-design}
library(survey)

survey_source <- ard


# Use phlebotomy weights because the analysis requires blood measurements.
# Keep participants with finite, positive weights.
survey_base <- survey_source %>%
  filter(is.finite(WTPH2YR), WTPH2YR > 0)

# Check that survey IDs and study eligibility are known for everyone in the survey sample.
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(survey_base$SDMVSTRA),
  !anyNA(survey_base$SDMVPSU),
  !anyNA(survey_base$eligible_study)
)

# Define the survey design before selecting eligible participants
# so variance estimates account for the full sample structure.
design_full <- svydesign(
  ids     = ~SDMVPSU,
  strata  = ~SDMVSTRA,
  weights = ~WTPH2YR,
  data    = survey_base,
  # PSU numbers repeat across strata, so identify each PSU by its stratum and number.
  nest    = TRUE
)

# Select eligible participants within the survey design
design <- subset(design_full, eligible_study)

# Check the expected participant and event counts, and confirm that
# participant IDs are in the same order as the saved ARD.
stopifnot(
  nrow(design$variables) == 3370,
  sum(design$variables$elevated_acr) == 417,
  identical(
  as.numeric(design$variables$SEQN),
  as.numeric(ard_reloaded$SEQN)
)
)
```


# Results

## Participant characteristics

Participants with elevated albuminuria were older, had higher mean HbA1c and systolic blood pressure, and had higher prevalences of diabetes and hypertension (Table 1). Race/ethnicity and smoking distributions also differed, while sex distribution and mean BMI were similar.



```{r table1}
library(gtsummary)

# Add readable category labels for Table 1, keeping the original variables.
ard_reloaded$elevated_acr_f <- factor(
  ard_reloaded$elevated_acr,
  levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  labels = c("ACR < 30 mg/g", "ACR ≥ 30 mg/g")
)

ard_reloaded$sex_f <- factor(
  ard_reloaded$RIAGENDR,
  levels = c(1, 2),
  labels = c("Male", "Female")
)

ard_reloaded$race_f <- factor(
  ard_reloaded$RIDRETH3,
  levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7),
  labels = c(
    "Mexican American", "Other Hispanic",
    "Non-Hispanic White", "Non-Hispanic Black",
    "Non-Hispanic Asian", "Other/Multi"
  )
)

ard_reloaded$diabetes_f <- factor(
  ard_reloaded$diabetes, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")
)

ard_reloaded$hypertension_f <- factor(
  ard_reloaded$hypertension, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")
)

ard_reloaded$obesity_f <- factor(
  ard_reloaded$obesity, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")
)

# Add the labelled variables to the survey design.
# Participant order was checked above so the labels match the correct records.
design <- update(
  design,
  elevated_acr_f = ard_reloaded$elevated_acr_f,
  sex_f = ard_reloaded$sex_f,
  race_f = ard_reloaded$race_f,
  diabetes_f = ard_reloaded$diabetes_f,
  hypertension_f = ard_reloaded$hypertension_f,
  obesity_f = ard_reloaded$obesity_f
)

# Compare participant characteristics by albuminuria status using survey weights.
tbl_svysummary(
  design,
  by = elevated_acr_f,
  include = c(
    RIDAGEYR, BMXBMI, LBXGH, mean_sbp, egfr,
    sex_f, race_f, smoking_status,
    diabetes_f, hypertension_f, obesity_f
  ),
  label = list(
    RIDAGEYR ~ "Age (years)",
    BMXBMI ~ "BMI (kg/m²)",
    LBXGH ~ "HbA1c (%)",
    mean_sbp ~ "Mean systolic BP (mmHg)",
    egfr ~ "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m²)",
    sex_f ~ "Sex",
    race_f ~ "Race/ethnicity",
    smoking_status ~ "Smoking status",
    diabetes_f ~ "Diabetes",
    hypertension_f ~ "Hypertension",
    obesity_f ~ "Obesity"
  ),
  # Report weighted means (SD) and percentages.
  statistic = list(
    all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
    all_categorical() ~ "{p}%"
  ),
  digits = list(
    all_continuous() ~ 1,
    all_categorical() ~ 1
  ),
  # Use available observations for each variable and omit missing-value rows.
  missing = "no"
) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  # Use tests that account for the survey design to compare the two groups.
  add_p(
    test = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "svy.t.test",
      all_categorical() ~ "svy.chisq.test"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Show actual participant counts in the headings, rather than weighted population        totals.
  modify_header(
    label = "**Characteristic**",
    all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}**  \nN = {n_unweighted}"
  ) %>%
  modify_footnote_header(
    footnote = paste(
      "Unweighted sample sizes; survey-weighted means (SD) and percentages.",
      "For diabetes, hypertension and obesity, percentages represent participants with the condition."
      
    ),
    columns = all_stat_cols(),
    replace = TRUE
  ) %>%
  modify_footnote_header(
    footnote = paste(
      "Design-based t-test for continuous variables;",
      "Rao–Scott adjusted Pearson’s χ² test for categorical variables."
    ),
    columns = p.value,
    replace = TRUE
  ) %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  modify_caption(
    "**Table 1.** Participant characteristics by elevated albuminuria status"
  )
```

## Prevalence of elevated albuminuria

```{r prevalence}
# Estimate prevalence using survey weights, with a logit-based confidence interval
# to keep the interval within 0–1.
prev    <- svyciprop(~elevated_acr, design, method = "logit", na.rm = TRUE)

# Extract the 95% confidence limits for the report.
prev_ci <- confint(prev)
```

The survey-weighted prevalence of elevated albuminuria was `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * as.numeric(prev))`% (95% CI `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * prev_ci[1])`–`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * prev_ci[2])`%).

## Associations with elevated albuminuria

```{r complete-case, include=FALSE}
# Scale age and systolic BP per 10 units, and BMI per 5 units,
# so the odds ratios describe meaningful increases. HbA1c stays per 1 percentage point.
design <- update(
  design,
  age_per10 = RIDAGEYR / 10,
  hba1c     = LBXGH,
  sbp_per10 = mean_sbp / 10,
  bmi_per5  = BMXBMI / 5
)

# Keep participants with all seven predictors available.
# Subset within the survey design to preserve the sampling structure.
design_cc <- subset(
  design,
  !is.na(age_per10) & !is.na(sex_f) & !is.na(race_f) &
  !is.na(hba1c) & !is.na(sbp_per10) & !is.na(bmi_per5) &
  !is.na(smoking_status)
)

# Count participants included in the model, those with elevated albuminuria,
# and those excluded because of missing predictors.
cc_summary <- tibble(
  Eligible_N      = 3370L,
  Complete_case_N = nrow(design_cc$variables),
  Events          = sum(design_cc$variables$elevated_acr),
  Excluded        = 3370L - nrow(design_cc$variables)
)

knitr::kable(
  cc_summary,
  caption = "Complete-case sample size for the primary logistic regression model"
)
```

The model included `r format(cc_summary$Complete_case_N, big.mark = ",")` complete-case participants, of whom `r cc_summary$Events` had elevated albuminuria.

```{r primary-model}
# Use Male and Non-Hispanic White as reference groups.
# Never smoker was already set as the smoking reference.
design_cc <- update(
  design_cc,
  sex_f  = relevel(sex_f, ref = "Male"),
  race_f = relevel(race_f, ref = "Non-Hispanic White")
)

# Estimate each predictor's association with elevated albuminuria,
# adjusting for the other predictors and the survey design.
model <- survey::svyglm(
  elevated_acr ~ age_per10 + sex_f + race_f + hba1c +
                 sbp_per10 + bmi_per5 + smoking_status,
  design = design_cc,
  # Use logistic regression without warnings about non-integer outcomes from survey        weights.
  family = quasibinomial()
)

# Convert model coefficients and confidence limits to adjusted odds ratios.
# Omit the intercept and format the results for the table.
library(broom)
library(scales)

or_table <- tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    OR      = round(estimate, 2),
    CI_low  = round(conf.low, 2),
    CI_high = round(conf.high, 2),
    p       = pvalue(p.value)
  ) %>%
  select(term, OR, CI_low, CI_high, p)

# Replace model term names with labels showing the units and reference groups.
or_table <- or_table %>%
  mutate(
    Characteristic = case_when(
      term == "age_per10"                   ~ "Age (per 10 years)",
      term == "sex_fFemale"                 ~ "Female (vs Male)",
      term == "race_fMexican American"      ~ "Mexican American (vs Non-Hispanic White)",
      term == "race_fOther Hispanic"        ~ "Other Hispanic (vs Non-Hispanic White)",
      term == "race_fNon-Hispanic Black"    ~ "Non-Hispanic Black (vs Non-Hispanic White)",
      term == "race_fNon-Hispanic Asian"    ~ "Non-Hispanic Asian (vs Non-Hispanic White)",
      term == "race_fOther/Multi"           ~ "Other/Multi (vs Non-Hispanic White)",
      term == "hba1c"                       ~ "HbA1c (per percentage point)",
      term == "sbp_per10"                   ~ "Systolic BP (per 10 mmHg)",
      term == "bmi_per5"                    ~ "BMI (per 5 kg/m²)",
      term == "smoking_statusFormer"        ~ "Former smoker (vs Never)",
      term == "smoking_statusCurrent"       ~ "Current smoker (vs Never)",
      TRUE ~ term
    )
  ) %>%
  select(Characteristic, OR, CI_low, CI_high, p)

knitr::kable(
  or_table,
  col.names = c("Characteristic", "Adjusted OR", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper", "p-value"),
  caption = "Adjusted odds ratios for elevated albuminuria from the primary survey-weighted logistic regression model",
  align = "lcccc"
)
```

After adjustment, older age, higher HbA1c and higher mean systolic blood pressure were associated with elevated albuminuria. Current smoking had an imprecise estimate (adjusted OR 1.73, 95% CI 1.00–3.00), and associations for sex, BMI, former smoking and race/ethnicity were not statistically significant.


```{r model-checks, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
# Calculate the number of albuminuria events per predictor parameter
# to assess how much data supports the model.
n_events  <- sum(design_cc$variables$elevated_acr)
# Count each estimated coefficient, including separate category comparisons,
# but exclude the intercept.
n_params  <- length(coef(model)) - 1          # exclude intercept
epv       <- n_events / n_params

tibble(
  Events     = n_events,
  Parameters = n_params,
  EPV        = round(epv, 1)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Events-per-variable assessment")
```

```{r linearity-check, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
# Add a squared term for one predictor at a time, keeping the other predictors unchanged.
# Test whether its association with the log odds of albuminuria shows curvature.

quad_age <- svyglm(
  elevated_acr ~ age_per10 + I(age_per10^2) + sex_f + race_f +
                 hba1c + sbp_per10 + bmi_per5 + smoking_status,
  design = design_cc, family = quasibinomial()
)

quad_hba1c <- svyglm(
  elevated_acr ~ age_per10 + sex_f + race_f +
                 hba1c + I(hba1c^2) + sbp_per10 + bmi_per5 + smoking_status,
  design = design_cc, family = quasibinomial()
)

quad_sbp <- svyglm(
  elevated_acr ~ age_per10 + sex_f + race_f +
                 hba1c + sbp_per10 + I(sbp_per10^2) + bmi_per5 + smoking_status,
  design = design_cc, family = quasibinomial()
)

quad_bmi <- svyglm(
  elevated_acr ~ age_per10 + sex_f + race_f +
                 hba1c + sbp_per10 + bmi_per5 + I(bmi_per5^2) + smoking_status,
  design = design_cc, family = quasibinomial()
)

# Extract each squared term's p-value to assess evidence of curvature.
quad_p <- tibble(
  Term = c("Age squared", "HbA1c squared", "Systolic BP squared", "BMI squared"),
  p_value = c(
    summary(quad_age)$coefficients["I(age_per10^2)", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    summary(quad_hba1c)$coefficients["I(hba1c^2)", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    summary(quad_sbp)$coefficients["I(sbp_per10^2)", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    summary(quad_bmi)$coefficients["I(bmi_per5^2)", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  )
)

knitr::kable(quad_p, digits = 3,
             caption = "Quadratic term tests for linearity of continuous predictors")
```

There were 33.4 events per estimated predictor parameter; exploratory tests found no evidence of quadratic departures from linearity in the log odds (all p > 0.13).

# Discussion

This project produced a documented, validated ARD for the planned survey-weighted analysis. The illustrative model identified associations with age, HbA1c and systolic blood pressure consistent with previous studies [@bryson_racial_2006; @nam_prevalence_2014].
Phenotypes combined self-reported diagnoses, medication use and measurements, and therefore depend on source accuracy and completeness; self-reports and single-examination measurements may misclassify phenotypes. Interpreting questionnaire routing allowed planned skips to be distinguished from unanswered questions, and an explicit indeterminate category preserved uncertainty rather than forcing classification. Requiring confirmed metabolic risk may nevertheless exclude participants with unrecognised or incompletely measured disease.

Retaining participants with missing covariates separated eligibility from model-specific exclusions and keeps the ARD usable for descriptive and alternative analyses. Complete-case regression excluded 3% of participants, which does not rule out selection bias; multiple imputation could be explored in sensitivity analysis. Because valid survey variance estimation requires the design to be declared before the eligible domain is selected, the supplied workflow reconstructs the full survey design from the public NHANES files; both the ARD and the analysis are therefore reproducible end to end.

Strengths include standardised NHANES measurements, participant-level linkage checks and retention of source variables alongside derived phenotypes, so every derivation can be audited. Validation went beyond structural checks to independent re-derivation and source reconciliation (Section 3.4), and the codebook documents every definition, unit and derivation rule.

The analysis used public-use, de-identified NHANES data collected under NCHS Ethics Review Board approval; no linkage to identifiable information was attempted.

The cross-sectional design precludes temporal or causal inference, and a single ACR measurement cannot confirm persistent albuminuria. Age top-coding at 80 years may overestimate eGFR in the oldest participants, affecting eligibility near the threshold. Requiring kidney measurements and confirmed metabolic risk limits generalisability, and residual confounding and other model misspecification remain possible.
